info.name: SiteReady NZ API
info.description:
# SiteReady NZ API

Run the whole collection in order (Collection Runner, or `newman run`). Every request checks its own status code and saves what the next one needs.

1. Start MongoDB and the API (`npm run dev` in `backend`). The API must answer on {{baseUrl}}.
2. Import this collection and the environment file, and choose the environment.
3. Click Run. Folders 1 to 7 create their own manager and staff accounts, so nothing needs setting up first.

Note: sign-in and sign-up allow 20 attempts per 15 minutes per address, and one full run uses 10 of them, so you can run it twice in a row. If you see 429 (too many attempts), restart the API or wait 15 minutes.

exec: // 1) Works out the dates used in the request bodies (today, +10 days, +400 days, -60 days).
// 2) Clears the cookie jar, so each request is judged only by the Authorization header it sets.

const day = (n) => { const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() + n); return [d.getFullYear(), String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0'), String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')].join('-'); }; // your local calendar day, not UTC

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Create the manager account for this run, sign in, and check the session. Run this folder first.

exec: pm.test('returns a token and the new user', () => { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(body.user.role).to.equal('manager'); });

request.description: Public sign-up always creates a MANAGER with their own workspace. A fresh email is made for every run.

exec: pm.test('200 OK with a JWT'.trim(), () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('the token is a JWT (three parts)', () => pm.expect(body.token.split('.')).to.have.length(3));
pm.test('is the manager we signed in as', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().user.email).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('managerEmail')));

item.name: 2. Staff
item.description: A manager creates a staff account, then the staff member signs in.

exec: pm.test('200 OK with an array'.trim(), () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('lists the staff member we just made', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map((p) => p.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('staffId')));

item.name: 3. Equipment (full CRUD)
item.description: Create, read, update and delete equipment. The server works out the status itself.

exec: pm.test('the server calculated the status: overdue', () => pm.expect(body.status).to.equal('overdue'));

request.description: Last checked 60 days ago, so the server calculates "overdue" (extinguishers need a check every 30 days).

exec: pm.test('200 OK with an array'.trim(), () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Staff may read equipment in their own workspace.
Checked today and expiring in 10 days, so the status becomes "due_soon".

item.name: 4. Inspections
item.description: Assign a check, do it as staff, upload it twice safely, and delete one that was not needed.

exec: pm.test('the checklist was built from the equipment type', () => pm.expect(body.items.length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('every question starts unanswered', () => pm.expect(body.items.every((i) => i.result === 'not_checked')).to.equal(true));
pm.test('200 OK with an array'.trim(), () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('the staff member sees the task', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map((i) => i._id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('inspectionId')));
const answers = items.map((item, index) => index === 0 ? { itemId: item.itemId, result: 'flag', notes: 'Gauge needle looks low' } : { itemId: item.itemId, result: 'pass', notes: '' });
pm.collectionVariables.set('submitBody', JSON.stringify({ inspectionId: pm.collectionVariables.get('inspectionId'), submissionId, items: answers }));

pm.collectionVariables.set('submitBodyOther', JSON.stringify({ inspectionId: pm.collectionVariables.get('inspectionId'), submissionId: 'postman-' + pm.collectionVariables.get('runId') + '-0002', items: answers }));
pm.test('the flagged answer and its note were saved', () => { pm.expect(body.items[0].result).to.equal('flag'); pm.expect(body.items[0].notes).to.equal('Gauge needle looks low'); });

request.description: One question is flagged (with a note), the rest pass.

item.name: POST /api/inspections/submit (the same upload again is safe)

exec: pm.test('still the same completed inspection', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b._id).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('inspectionId')); pm.expect(b.status).to.equal('completed'); });

request.description: A phone that lost signal mid-upload will retry. The same submissionId must succeed without a second record.

item.name: POST /api/inspections/submit (a DIFFERENT upload for a finished check)
POST /api/inspections (a second check, assigned by mistake)
POST /api/inspections (a third check, left open on purpose)

request.description: Left open so you can see it removed automatically when its equipment is deleted (folder 7).

item.name: 5. Push notifications
item.description: Subscribe a device, send a message, run the automatic checks. The device here is a made-up address, so delivery is not expected.

exec: pm.test('200 OK (503 if push is not set up on this server)'.trim(), () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('only the PUBLIC key is ever returned', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.publicKey).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include('private'); });

request.description: Only real browser push services are accepted, so the server can never be tricked into calling an internal address.

exec: pm.test('reports devices, delivered and a plain message', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.devices).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(b.delivered).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(b.message).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test('returns the counts', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.reminders).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(b.lateAlerts).to.be.a('number'); });

item.name: 6. Error codes and attack attempts
item.description: Every error status the rubric asks for (400, 401, 403, 404, 409), plus NoSQL-injection attempts that must be refused.

item.name: 400: id is not a valid MongoDB id
401: unknown email gives the SAME message

exec: pm.test('same message as a wrong password', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('wrongPasswordMessage')));

request.description: The answer must be identical to "wrong password", so nobody can find out which emails have accounts.

item.name: 400: NoSQL injection, operator in the email

request.description: {"$gt": ""} would match every account if it reached the database. It is refused before that.

item.name: 400: NoSQL injection, array as the email
400: NoSQL injection, operator as the password
400: an object as the equipment name
200: query-string operators are ignored (only your own workspace comes back)

exec: pm.test('every item belongs to our workspace', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().every((e) => e.organisationId === pm.collectionVariables.get('orgId'))).to.equal(true));

item.name: 201: injected status and workspace are ignored (mass assignment)

exec: pm.test('status was NOT taken from the request', () => pm.expect(body.status).to.not.equal('expired'));
pm.test('workspace was NOT taken from the request', () => pm.expect(body.organisationId).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('orgId')));

request.description: The body tries to set status "expired" and someone else's workspace. The server decides both itself.

item.name: 7. Delete equipment, then sign out
item.description: Deleting equipment also removes its open checks, and keeps finished ones as history.

item.name: GET /api/inspections (history survives, open checks are gone)

exec: pm.test('the finished check is kept as history, showing "Removed equipment"', () => { pm.expect(done).to.exist; pm.expect(done.equipmentId.name).to.equal('Removed equipment'); });
pm.test('the check that was still open was removed with its equipment', () => pm.expect(list.map((i) => i._id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('thirdInspectionId')));
